record.original_question:
Characterize all symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomials of
degree d in n variables. In particular, determine
whether every such polynomial p can be represented in the form p(z1,
..., zn) = η(z1A, ..., znA) for some d×d positive
semidefinite matrix A, where η is the mixed-determinant-type
polynomial defined in the source.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n,d be positive integers. A polynomial p ∈ ℝ[z_1,…,z_n] is called real stable if p has no zeros in the open upper half-plane product, i.e. p(z_1,…,z_n) ≠ 0 whenever Im(z_j) > 0 for every j = 1,…,n. Call p symmetric if it is invariant under every permutation of its variables, and homogeneous of degree d if p(t z_1,…,t z_n) = t^d p(z_1,…,z_n).

For d×d real symmetric matrices B_1,…,B_n, let
   η(B_1,…,B_n) := det(B_1 + B_2 + ⋯ + B_n),
viewed as a polynomial in the entries of the B_i; equivalently, expanding by multilinearity of the determinant, η is the "mixed-determinant" polynomial
   η(B_1,…,B_n) = ∑_{(j_1,…,j_d) ∈ {1,…,n}^d} det[ B_{j_1}^{(1)} | B_{j_2}^{(2)} | ⋯ | B_{j_d}^{(d)} ],
where B_j^{(k)} denotes the k-th column of B_j.

(a) Characterize all symmetric, real stable, homogeneous polynomials of degree d in n variables.

(b) Decide whether every such polynomial p admits a representation
   p(z_1,…,z_n) = η(z_1 A, z_2 A, …, z_n A) = det\bigl((z_1 + z_2 + ⋯ + z_n) A\bigr) \cdot (\text{appropriate normalization}),
or more generally
   p(z_1,…,z_n) = η(z_1 A,…,z_n A)
for some d × d positive semidefinite real symmetric matrix A.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search for a characterization of symmetric real stable homogeneous polynomials via mixed-determinant representations with a single PSD matrix did not produce conclusive evidence of a resolution. No clear publication confirming a full characterization or a counterexample was located.

status_evidence.title: Real Stable Polynomials: Description and Application — Theo McKenzie
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of real stable polynomials and determinantal-type constructions.
status_evidence.claim: General background on real stable polynomials; no characterization of symmetric ones via η is given.

status_evidence.title: Positive Semidefinite Univariate Matrix Polynomials (arXiv:1707.08261)
status_evidence.snippet: Sum-of-squares-type representations of PSD matrix polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not address symmetric real stable homogeneous polynomial characterization.
